Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x - y - 5 z &=6 \\ x + 2 y + 4 z &=-3 \\ - 2 x + 2 y + 10 z &=-12\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.
other_records.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -5 & 6 \\ 1 & 2 & 4 & -3 \\ -2 & 2 & 10 & -12\end{array}\right]
$$

First reduce the matrix to row echelon form, making each pivot equal to $1$.

$$
R_{2}:=R_{2}+\left(-1\right)R_{1}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -5 & 6 \\ 0 & 3 & 9 & -9 \\ -2 & 2 & 10 & -12\end{array}\right]
$$



$$
R_{3}:=R_{3}+\left(2\right)R_{1}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -5 & 6 \\ 0 & 3 & 9 & -9 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$



$$
R_{2}:=\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)R_{2}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -5 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only.

$$
R_{1}:=R_{1}+\left(1\right)R_{2}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

other_records.:question/problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2 x - 5 y + 11 z &=4 \\ - 2 x + 10 y - 16 z &=-4 \\ x - 5 y + 8 z &=2\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
other_records.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & -5 & 11 & 4 \\ -2 & 10 & -16 & -4 \\ 1 & -5 & 8 & 2\end{array}\right]
$$

First reduce the matrix to row echelon form, making each pivot equal to $1$.

$$
R_{1}\leftrightarrow R_{3}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -5 & 8 & 2 \\ -2 & 10 & -16 & -4 \\ 2 & -5 & 11 & 4\end{array}\right]
$$



$$
R_{2}:=R_{2}+\left(2\right)R_{1}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -5 & 8 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & -5 & 11 & 4\end{array}\right]
$$



$$
R_{3}:=R_{3}+\left(-2\right)R_{1}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -5 & 8 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & -5 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$



$$
R_{2}\leftrightarrow R_{3}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -5 & 8 & 2 \\ 0 & 5 & -5 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$



$$
R_{2}:=\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)R_{2}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -5 & 8 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only.

$$
R_{1}:=R_{1}+\left(5\right)R_{2}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x + 3 z &=2 \\ y - z &=0 \\ 0 &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The final equation is $0=0$, so it imposes no restriction. The basic variables are $x$ and $y$, and the free variable is $z$. Find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z$. Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=2 - 3 z \\ y &=z \\ z &=z\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $z$ is an arbitrary real number. In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2 - 3 z \\ z \\ z\end{bmatrix},\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty )
$$

Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x + 2 y + 2 z &=-2 \\ - 3 x - 6 y - 6 z &=6 \\ 2 x + 5 y + 6 z &=-6\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
other_records.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 2 & -2 \\ -3 & -6 & -6 & 6 \\ 2 & 5 & 6 & -6\end{array}\right]
$$

First reduce the matrix to row echelon form, making each pivot equal to $1$.

$$
R_{2}:=R_{2}+\left(3\right)R_{1}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 5 & 6 & -6\end{array}\right]
$$



$$
R_{3}:=R_{3}+\left(-2\right)R_{1}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -2\end{array}\right]
$$



$$
R_{2}\leftrightarrow R_{3}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only.

$$
R_{1}:=R_{1}+\left(-2\right)R_{2}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x - 2 z &=2 \\ y + 2 z &=-2 \\ 0 &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The final equation is $0=0$, so it imposes no restriction. The basic variables are $x$ and $y$, and the free variable is $z$. Find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z$. Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=2 z + 2 \\ y &=- 2 z - 2 \\ z &=z\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $z$ is an arbitrary real number. In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2 z + 2 \\ - 2 z - 2 \\ z\end{bmatrix},\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty )
$$
